test_cases.title: Toggle Chat Panel Visibility
test_cases.objective: Verify that the toggle button correctly shows and hides the chat panel.
preconditions: ChatBubble component is rendered in the application
No prior panel state is assumed
steps: Render the ChatBubble component
Locate the toggle button using selector "button.btn.btn-primary.rounded-circle.d-flex.justify-content-center.align-items-center"
Click the toggle button
Assert that the chat panel (form.p-2) becomes visible
Click the toggle button again
Assert that the chat panel is hidden

mock_strategy.notes: No network calls are involved in this interaction.

pass_when: Panel visibility toggles correctly on each click
fail_when: Panel does not change visibility as expected

test_cases.title: Submit New Chat Message
test_cases.objective: Verify that submitting a new chat message via the form works correctly.
steps: Render the ChatBubble component
If the panel is hidden, click the toggle button to show it
Locate the input field using selector "input.form-control.form-control-sm.mb-2" and enter the sample message "Hello world"
Locate the submit button using selector "button.btn.btn-primary.btn-sm.w-100" and click it
Mock the ../api/chatApi endpoint to return a successful response
Assert that a success indicator appears (e.g., no error message)

mock_strategy.notes: Mock a successful API response to isolate UI behavior.

pass_when: Message is sent without error and UI reflects success
fail_when: Submission fails or an error message is displayed

test_cases.title: Reject Empty Message Submission
test_cases.objective: Verify that submitting an empty message does not send a chat.
steps: Render the ChatBubble component
Ensure the panel is visible
Enter an empty string into the input field
Click the submit button
Mock the ../api/chatApino request is made
Assert that an appropriate validation message is displayed or no API call occurs

mock_strategy.notes: Verify that no network request is sent when the message is empty.

pass_when: No API request is sent and validation feedback is shown
fail_when: Empty message is sent or no validation occurs

test_cases.title: Validate successful login with valid credentials
test_cases.objective: Verify that the LoginForm accepts valid email and password inputs and submits the form correctly.
preconditions: User is on the page containing the LoginForm.
No mock server is required for this test case as no external API calls are made.
steps: 1. Navigate to the page URL where the LoginForm is rendered.
2. Verify that the email input element with selector 'input[data-testid="email-input"]' is present and enabled.
3. Type the email value 'test@example.com' into the email input field.
4. Verify that the email input's value attribute equals 'test@example.com'.
5. Verify that the password input element with selector 'input[data-testid="password-input"]' is present and enabled.
6. Type the password value 'Password123' into the password input field.
7. Verify that the password input's value attribute equals 'Password123' and that the input type remains masked.
8. Verify that the login button with selector 'button[data-testid="login-button"]' is enabled.
9. Click the login button.
10. Verify that the form submission results in navigation to the expected dashboard page or displays a success message.

mock_strategy.notes: No external API calls are made; no mocking required.

pass_when: The email and password values are correctly entered and retained.
The login button becomes clickable after both fields are filled.
Form submission leads to the expected post‑login UI (e.g., dashboard or success message).
fail_when: Any selector is not found or not interactable.
The email or password field does not accept the entered value.
The login button remains disabled after both fields are populated.
Form submission does not result in navigation or success indication.
